rv.q: I feel there is real potential here, but it is disappointing that it left so little of a mark on me.
Other than this, the evening is neither offensive nor intriguing, but largely forgettable, a shame given what it might have been.
Holy Fool works well in its hybrid state between autobiography and thriller.
Whilst some scenes are a little drawn out, this is an interesting look at one man's struggle to continue making music, and stay alive, in turbulent times.
There is much to admire here: a strong ensemble and a story that places artistic freedom, morality and survival under uncomfortable scrutiny.

Underground resistance and the human spirit is the story told here in an extremely well created and performed piece of work, with strong character acting and wry, comic moments to leaven the harsh story.
